Unlike standard Vector Quantization which maps vectors to a single codebook, R-VQ decomposes the quantization error across multiple stages, allowing for higher precision with smaller individual codebooks [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the method adopts Residual Vector Quantization (R-VQ) which 'cascades L stages of VQ with codebook size C'. It further explains that the reconstructed vector is the sum of selected codes from each stage, effectively decomposing the quantization process across multiple stages. The text also notes that this approach is used to reduce computational complexity and GPU memory (storage reduced significantly, e.g., from 746 MB to 48.8 MB), which supports the claim of achieving higher precision/efficiency with smaller individual codebooks compared to standard VQ.
supported
